suggestions.assertion: The report identifies that FLAT5 ignores the 2000-cent subtotal rule as a spec gap (objective: report_mentions_threshold_gap)
suggestions.reason: The objective check only greps the report for the substring '2000'. A report that merely restated the spec's acceptance criterion text ('AC2: FLAT5 applies when subtotal >= 2000') without ever concluding the implementation fails to enforce it would also satisfy this check. This run clears the bar with real margin (it proves negative totals via an executed probe), but the assertion itself doesn't distinguish a genuine gap-finding from a coincidental mention of the number.

suggestions.assertion: The verdict is not 'ready to merge' (objective: report_not_ready_to_merge)
suggestions.reason: This is a bare substring match on 'not ready'. A report whose actual verdict was 'ready to merge' could still trip this check with an unrelated phrase (e.g., 'the tests are not ready-made, but the branch is ready to merge'). Anchoring the check to an explicit verdict line (e.g., a 'Ready to merge?' Q/A pattern, which this run conveniently uses) would make it more discriminating.

No expectation rewards or requires executed proof over static claims. This run distinguished itself by writing throwaway vitest probes against the real src/pricing.ts to demonstrate the FLAT5 negative-total bug and the case-sensitivity bug with actual output, rather than just reading the code and asserting a gap. A future expectation like 'the report backs at least one defect claim with executed/observed output, not just static code reading' would reward this kind of rigor and catch reviews that guess wrong from source alone.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 expectations pass with genuine, non-superficial evidence — the report demonstrates rather than merely asserts the required findings (e.g., an executed probe proving FLAT5 yields negative totals). Four of the five automated objective checks are plain substring/keyword matches, though, so they would also pass a much shallower report that name-drops the right files/numbers without real analysis; consider tightening report_mentions_threshold_gap and report_not_ready_to_merge as noted above. Expectation 5 (standards vs. spec separation) has no objective check and was graded purely from the transcript; it passed on a genuine, dedicated 'Standards axis' vs. 'Spec axis' split, but an automated structural check (e.g., presence of two distinctly-headed sections) would remove reliance on manual grading for it.
